entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gnaeus Cornelius Scipio Hispanus (unknown–200 BCE) was a Roman politician and the prominent leader of the Scipiones branch of the gens Cornelia.

As a skilled military commander, Scipio Hispanus played a crucial role in the Second Punic War, leading Roman forces to victory against Carthage in the Battle of Zama in 202 BCE. This decisive battle not only secured Roman dominance over the Mediterranean but also cemented Scipio's reputation as a brilliant tactician.

Scipio's achievements extended beyond the battlefield, as he implemented various reforms in Rome, including the creation of a new system of taxation and the establishment of a permanent Roman army. His work laid the groundwork for future Roman expansion and the rise of the Roman Republic.

Despite his significant contributions to Roman history, Scipio's legacy was marred by controversy, as he was accused of corruption and abuse of power. Nevertheless, his impact on Roman politics and warfare remains a topic of interest among historians and scholars.

Scipio's life serves as a testament to the enduring power of Roman leadership, as he navigated the complexities of Roman politics and military strategy to achieve greatness.
